set.affordability_requirement: State density bonus thresholds (County Code 18.107.170 implements Gov. Code 65915 for housing developments as defined in state law). Affordable housing agreement required for any bonus, incentive, parking reduction or waiver: rental target units affordable at least 55 years (or longer if financing requires), for-sale units 45 years with sale to a qualified nonprofit if no income-qualified buyer within 180 days (18.107.180(E)-(G)). Requests are filed with the first discretionary permit with detailed submittals; incentives and waivers may be denied only on specified written findings (18.107.180(B)-(C)). On-site inclusionary units can count toward the bonus; paying in-lieu fees does not (18.107.170(D)(3)).

set.typical_award_size: Negative finding. Vacaville has no housing trust fund, inclusionary requirement, in-lieu fee or affordable housing fee waiver. Chapter 11.01 (Development Impact Fees, amended by Ord. 2005 on Aug 12, 2025) has no affordable housing exemption; it lets any applicant defer fees to final inspection under a recorded lien agreement (11.01.080), cuts the traffic impact fee 25 percent for multifamily projects of at least 20.1 units per acre in the Allison PDA within one half mile of the Vacaville Transportation Center (11.01.070(F)), exempts ADUs under 750 sq ft, and lets Council adopt fee deferral or reduction policies by resolution (11.01.100(B)); no such policy was found. set.typical_award_size: Affordable Housing Fee Reduction Pilot Program, adopted by City Council Sept 15, 2026 (Legistar matter 352-2026; Resolutions R2026-111 and R2026-112). Building permit fees (fee numbers 2.1.6-2.1.10 multifamily, 2.1.26-2.1.30 single family, 2.1.36 ADU) are reduced 100 percent for very low and extremely low income units, 75 percent for low income units, and 50 percent for moderate income units (120% AMI) and ADUs or JADUs of 749 sq ft or less; this replaces Resolution R2021-119 (flat 50 percent). Development impact fees (Fire and Paramedic, Street Improvement, Park Development, Park Land Dedication, Orchard Avenue, North Jefferson, High-Priority Improvement Payback, Big Ranch Road, Lone Oak Drainage) are reduced 100 percent for very low and extremely low income units and 75 percent for low income units, capped at 250 very low and 250 low income units, first come first served. Staff estimated about $8,622 per very low income unit and $6,275 per low income unit in impact fee savings. Separately, NMC 15.94.040 lets affordable housing impact fees be deferred to final inspection or certificate of occupancy under a recorded secured building agreement.
set.per_unit_cap: No dollar cap per unit; impact fee reductions capped at 250 very low income and 250 low income units in total.
set.affordability_requirement: Units must be deed restricted at least 55 years (rental) or 45 years (for-sale) under an NMC 15.94.080 affordable housing agreement, use HCD income limits unless a funding source requires otherwise, and be reportable on the City's RHNA annual report; units in an approved alternative equivalent to paying affordable housing impact fees do not qualify. Building permit reductions reach moderate income (120% AMI); impact fee reductions apply only to low, very low and extremely low income units.
set.cycle_notes: Pilot applies to building permits applied for or issued between July 1, 2026 and December 31, 2028, or until the 250 very low and 250 low income unit caps are reached. Construction must begin within one year of permit issuance or the permit is rescinded (impact fees) or the fees are added back (building permit fees). The Director will issue an administrative regulation and application process.
set.next_deadline: Building permits must be applied for or issued by December 31, 2028, or until the unit caps are reached.
set.layering_notes: Fee relief now covers most City impact fees for lower-income units and is routinely combined with affordable housing impact fee and TOT loans. The Director may limit reductions to projects where they move the project to construction and no other funding gap exists. Napa Valley Unified School District and Napa Sanitation District fees are outside the City's control. Waived or reduced fees can count as public funds under Labor Code 1720(b)(4), so confirm with counsel. Resolution text read from the staff-attached drafts (R2026-XX) on Legistar; the matter history records adoption on Sept 15, 2026 with enactment numbers R2026-111 and R2026-112.
set.audit_note: NC audit Nov 10, 2026: Corrected from the R2021-119 flat 50 percent building permit reduction to the Sept 15, 2026 pilot program (Legistar matter 352-2026, R2026-111 and R2026-112), which rescinds R2021-119 and adds impact fee reductions.
